text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) usually causes no signs or symptoms at all, which is why doctors often call it the "silent killer".
snippet_highlighted_words: no signs or symptoms at all

text_blocks.snippet: Most people feel completely fine even if their blood pressure is high. However, if your blood pressure spikes to dangerous levels (above 180/120 mm Hg), you may experience sudden warning signs.

list.snippet: Severe headaches: A sudden, pounding headache that feels worse than usual.
Vision changes: Blurry vision, double vision, or temporary loss of sight.
Shortness of breath: Trouble catching your breath during light activity or while resting.
Chest pain: Tightness or pressure in the chest area.
Dizziness: Feeling lightheaded, woozy, or unsteady.

text_blocks.snippet: A blood pressure reading over 180/120 mm Hg combined with symptoms like confusion, severe chest pain, or stroke signs is a medical emergency. You can learn more about these warning signs from the American Heart Association or review clinical details at the Mayo Clinic. Measuring your blood pressure regularly is the only way to catch the condition early.
